text:
**Short answer:** for a lot of cells at once, get a 16-bay charger with independent slots. I'd start with the Tenergy TN438. If you'd rather start smaller, the Tenergy TN480U 8-bay is the one model where I have a price and a buy link.

**16-bay options**
- **Tenergy TN438 (16 bays):** charges AA and AAA NiMH/NiCd in any mix. It has an LCD showing each cell's status, protection against overcharge, overheating, short circuits and reverse polarity, and an eight-hour timer ([Electronics Advisor](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/)). It's my pick because of the per-cell readout and the protections.
- **BONAI 16-Bay:** takes any number of cells in any slot and mixes AA and AAA. It runs on 110-240V AC at 250-500 mA per port and has LED status per port. It won't charge alkaline or lithium cells ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/)).
- **POWEROWL 16-Bay:** 16 independent channels with a four-stage charge (pre-charge, quick, float, trickle) ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/)).
- **CITYORK 16-Bay:** smart LCD with real-time status and a ventilated design for heat ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/)).

**8-bay option with a price: Tenergy TN480U, $23.99**
- It charges 8 AA or AAA cells, mixed, at 500 mA per AA and 250 mA per AAA, with a per-slot LCD and bad-cell detection.
- It needs a 5V 2A USB adapter, which isn't included. On a 1A source, five or more AA cells drop to 250 mA each.
- The seller's listing doesn't confirm that every bay is fully independent.
- Buy: [Tenergy TN480U on Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger) (affiliate link; source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-high-capacity-aa-aaa-nimh-battery-charger-8-bay-16-bay-independent-channels)).
- Two of these would give you 16 bays for about $48 plus two USB adapters.

**Caveats**
- The Electronics Advisor pages are affiliate roundups, not hands-on tests. Check recent buyer reviews before you commit.
- The search results didn't include prices or direct purchase links for the 16-bay models, so search the model name on Amazon or Tenergy's store.
- Charge time grows with the number of cells, and a fully loaded 16-bay unit draws more power.
- If you want high-capacity cells to go with it, Dealectric lists a Tenergy Premium PRO 2,800 mAh AA 20-pack at $42.99 ([link](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack), affiliate).

If you tell me roughly how many cells you charge at a time and your budget, I can narrow this down.
